Title: Patrologiae graecae tomus CL: Gregorius Palamas, Constantinus Harmenopulus, Theophanes Nicaenus, alii. Gregorii Palamae, Thessalonicensis archiepiscopi, Opera omnia theologica, homiletica, hagiographica, polemica, ascetica. Accedunt Gregorii Sinaitae, Constantini Harmenopuli nomophylacis, Macarii Chrysocephali Philadelphiensis metropolitae, Joannis Calecae CPolitani patriarchae, Theophanis Nicaeni archiepiscopi, Nicolai Cabasilae Thessalonicensis quae supersunt. Gregorii tomus prior, caeterorum tomus unicus
Creator: Gregory Palamas (c. 1296-1359), archbishop of Thessalonica; with Gregory of Sinai, Constantine Harmenopoulos, Macarius Chrysocephalus, John Calecas, Theophanes of Nicaea and Nicholas Cabasilas; Greek texts with parallel Latin, edited by J.-P. Migne
Publisher: Paris: J.-P. Migne (Petit-Montrouge), Patrologiae cursus completus, Series graeca, tomus 150
Publication Date: 1865
Rights: Public Domain
Rights basis: the imprint year is 1865: another scan of this volume (archive.org item bim_early-english-books-1641-1700_patrologiae-cursus-completus-_1865_150) reads 1865 on both title pages, and the list of Migne's volumes printed in tomus CLXI (file line 110872 of the Bessarion volume vendored beside this one) reads 'CL (1865)'. This scan's own OCR reads '1863' at file line 248. Either year is far before 1930. Host record: date field 1857 (the series start), possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT.
Language: grc (Greek with parallel or following Latin translation; the Latin and Greek share the OCR file; see the content note)
Source: Internet Archive item patrologicursus01migngoog (archive.org/details/patrologicursus01migngoog), full-text file patrologicursus01migngoog_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the Library thread, October 2026.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the Library thread; the OCR text follows it unchanged. Nothing was stripped, normalised, corrected, re-spaced or retyped (the long s glyph occurs 0 times and was left as found). The Google Books boilerplate page at the head of the OCR is left in place. The file is 3763780 bytes, 2699072 characters and 74402 lines. OCR quality sampled at the title pages and at about 5%, 50% and 95% of the file (lines 3720, 37201 and 70681): Greek polytonic mostly clean with occasional chi for kappa and stray Latin letters; Latin clean with ordinary OCR slips.
Content note: Tomus 150 as the volume's own ELENCHUS lists it: Constantine Harmenopoulos (including his tract against Palamas); Macarius Chrysocephalus; John Calecas (two homilies); Theophanes of Nicaea; Nicholas Cabasilas (the Commentary on the Divine Liturgy in Greek and Latin, the Life in Christ in Latin, a sermon against usurers, the encomium of St Theodora); and Gregory Palamas (the Hagioritic Tome 'pro Hesychastis', De Hesychastis, the 150 physical, theological, moral and practical chapters, letters, homilies and the Prosopopoeiae); a section of Greek opinions on Palamas (Akindynos's iambs, Andrew of Kolossai's dialogue, the tome of condemnation, Harmenopoulos on the Palamite heresy, a patriarchal tome against the Palamite synod, David the monk on the quarrel of Barlaam and Palamas); then Gregory of Sinai (ascetic chapters and the short tracts on quiet and the two modes of prayer, from file line 84364). The Life in Christ appears in Latin only; its Greek is in Gass (vendored separately). The volume also carries Migne's editorial notes in Latin. Greek and Latin columns run side by side, so the OCR interleaves them line by line in the biblical-canons and Palamas sections.

Theophanes Ill, episcopus Nicenus, circa an. 1337, diu post exortum schisma floruit, 
ut bene docet P. Lequien, Oriens Christian., t. I, p. 652, non sutem seculo VIII, ut pro-

ad Theopbanem, sub imperatore Theophilo impio iconoclasta, fortissimut martyrem, nou 
δὰ Theophanem Nicenum, referenda sunt. 

Auctor harum epistolarum passim insinuat Niceam ab infidelibus esse occupatam, 
&deo ut sedem suam adire non possit, aut vix possit. Conqueritur eo quod oves su& 
supra modum vexenutur, et eas hortatur, prolato Jobi exemplo, ad tolerandas cum pa- 
tientia etiam maximas tribulationes. Alicubi refellit heresim Palamitarum , que seeculo 
XIV tandem exorta est. Hec autem omoia respondent &tati quam Theophani ossignamus, 
sed opinioni Consalvi Ponce de Leon ex adverso opponuntur. “ 

Theophanis scribendi ratio est simplex et humilis, etsi oinni nobilitate non careat. 

In prima epistola promotionem suam gregi suo annuntiat, et quia grex ille versetur in 
urbe captiva et oppressa, ad quam accedere nequit, patientiam et fortitudinem animi. in 
tentationibus precipue commendat. Deinde ostendit bareticos sedulo fugiendos esse, et 
Palamitas refellit, Secunda epistola fere in eodem argumento evolvendo -tota versatur. 
Eidem accedit gratiarum actio, eo quod liberatus fuerit ἃ peste et a morte. Tertia epistola 
exponenda sacre doctrine et commendande discipline ecclesiastice fere integra adhtbe- 
tur. Auctor sacerdotes sibi subjectos alloquens, de incarnatione Domini, de regeneratione 
fidelium et de divinis sacramentis copiose disserit. Deinde potestatem spiritualem saeer- 
dotum pulcherrimis verbis commendat, transubstantiationem agnoscit, ac de vita sacere 
dotali, quid scilicet sacerdoti faciendum, quid fogiendum sit, prolixe enarrat.

NICOLAI CABASILJE 
DE DIVINO ALTARIS SACRIFICIO. 


(Gentiano Herreto Aurelio interprete.)

144. Essentia Dei nullatenus nuncupari potest, 
cum sit omnino incomprehensa. Nominatur igitur 
ex omnibus suis operationibus ; et nullum ibi no- 
minum ab alio significatione differt. Singulis enim 
et omnibus nihil aliud vocatur quam absconditum 
illud miuime notum quid sit. De operationibus vero 
nomina singula diverssm habent significationem ; 
quis enim nescit ase invicem distincta esse crea- 
tionem, dominium, judicium, prowentiam, et 
nostram ex gratia Dei adoptionem ? Qui ergo nstu- 
rales illas Dei operationes, utpote ab invicem et a 
natura divina distinctas, dicunt creatas, nonne 
Deum ad creaturam deprimunt? Nam creata, et 
gubernata, et judicata, et generatim omnia hujus- 
modi sunt creature; non vero ipse Creator, et 
Dominus, et Judex, nec ipsum judicium, et domi- 
nium, et creatio, quz sunt naturales ipsius modi.
